title: Acute Changes in Pulmonary Oxygenation After Nimodipine Administration in Patients With Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage: A Retrospective Dose-Level Observational Study
summary:
Nimodipine is a medication routinely used in patients with subarachnoid hemorrhage caused by a ruptured intracranial aneurysm. In clinical practice, there may be concern that, in addition to its hemodynamic effects, nimodipine could impair pulmonary oxygen uptake.
The aim of this retrospective study is to investigate whether oxygenation deteriorates shortly after the administration of nimodipine and whether any observed changes depend on the administered dose.
For this purpose, routinely collected data from patients with aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage will be analyzed. For individual administrations of nimodipine, a value from an arterial blood gas analysis obtained before drug administration will be compared with a value obtained after administration. The ratio of arterial partial pressure of oxygen to the inspired oxygen concentration will be used as a measure of pulmonary oxygenation.
Only data already collected as part of routine clinical care will be analyzed. The study will not involve any additional examinations, blood sampling, or changes to patient treatment.

interventions.name: Retrospective analysis of patients treated for aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage who received nimodipine during intensive care treatment.
